title: Others building the how of self-government
intro: County Commons does one job: it makes your county's money and questions plain. It is not the only group working on the how of self-government. These organizations teach people, for free, how to read a law, get a public record, weigh a decision together, or put a question on the ballot. We point to them because the work is bigger than any one county — and because knowing how the machine works is the first step to steering it.
neutrality_note: We link by method, not by cause. Every group here helps people learn how self-government works — the how-to, not the what-to. None is listed for a policy it favors or a party it prefers, and a link is not our endorsement of anything they argue elsewhere. We checked each one: it had to be real, still running, and nonpartisan. If you find one has drifted into pushing a policy or a party, tell us and we'll take it down. That's the line — and it's the same line we hold ourselves to.
closing: Know a nonpartisan group that teaches people how to change the law — the method, not the cause? Send it in and we'll verify it the same way we verified these.

groups.category: See what the law says, and what's changing
groups.blurb: Bills, ballot measures, and voting records — public, searchable, and free.

orgs.name: Ballotpedia
orgs.what: Look up any election, official, or ballot measure — and how your state's initiative process works.

orgs.name: Open States
orgs.what: Find your state legislators and track state bills by address or keyword.

orgs.name: GovTrack
orgs.what: Track federal bills and see how your members of Congress actually vote.

orgs.name: Congress.gov
orgs.what: Read the official text and status of any bill in Congress.

orgs.name: National Conference of State Legislatures
orgs.what: Learn how state legislatures and ballot measures work, state by state. Nonpartisan by charter.

groups.blurb: The law already gives you the right to see how decisions get made. These help you use it.

orgs.name: MuckRock
orgs.what: File, track, and share public-records (FOIA) requests to any government agency.

orgs.name: National Freedom of Information Coalition
orgs.what: State-by-state open-records help, hotlines, and sample request letters.

orgs.name: Reporters Committee — Open Government Guide
orgs.what: Free guides to the open-records and open-meetings law in every state.

groups.category: Put a question on the ballot yourself
groups.blurb: In many states, citizens can write a law and vote on it directly. Here's how that actually works.

orgs.name: Ballotpedia — Laws governing the initiative process
orgs.what: The exact signatures, deadlines, and filing rules to put a measure on your state's ballot.

groups.category: Decide together — deliberation and citizen panels
groups.blurb: Tested ways for a group of ordinary people to study a question and reach a fair decision together.

orgs.name: Healthy Democracy
orgs.what: Panels of everyday voters study a ballot measure and write a fair fact sheet for the rest of us.

orgs.name: DemocracyNext
orgs.what: Helps cities set up citizens' assemblies where randomly chosen residents make real decisions.

orgs.name: Stanford Deliberative Democracy Lab
orgs.what: Research on how opinion changes when a random group gets good facts and talks it through.

orgs.name: Participedia
orgs.what: A free library of real-world examples of communities trying public participation.

orgs.name: Polis (Computational Democracy Project)
orgs.what: A free tool that gathers a crowd's views in their own words and shows where people actually agree.

orgs.name: Decidim
orgs.what: Open-source software a town uses to run proposals, budgets, and votes with residents.

orgs.name: CONSUL Democracy
orgs.what: Free software for debates, citizen proposals, and participatory budgeting on a government's own site.

orgs.name: Arkansas Secretary of State — Initiatives & Referenda
orgs.what: The official Arkansas steps to petition and qualify a ballot measure.

orgs.name: Arkansas Press Association — FOIA Handbook
orgs.what: How to request Arkansas public records and attend open meetings. Written with the Attorney General.
